paper.title: Phy-Q as a measure for physical reasoning intelligence
paper.authors: Xue, Pinto, Gamage, Nikonova, Zhang, Renz

figures_with_numbers.Fig4_local_broad_gen.PNG: Fig. 4 (a: per-scenario broad-gen bars; b: table of Local gen./Broad gen. means)

paper.readme_result_tables: none (README.md has scenario descriptions, setup and the play-data column description; no result tables)

phyq_definition.text: We calculate Phy-Q of an agent using the results of our \textit{broad generalization} evaluation
When calculating the Phy-Q we exclude the first two scenarios: single force and multiple forces
where $P_{n,m}$ is the average pass rate of subject \textit{n} in the $m^{th}$ scenario. $\sigma_{human,m}$ is the standard deviation of human pass rate in scenario $m$

human_average_pass_rate.text: The average pass rate is calculated as 100\% if the player passes at the first attempt and if the player passes at the fifth attempt, the pass rate is 20\%.

heuristic_pass_rate.text: Due to the randomness in the heuristic agents, we allow them to have five attempts per task and calculate the task pass rate by averaging the result over these five attempts

the agents were tested on the same $20\%$ of the test tasks from each task template (1500 tasks in total) used for the D-DDQN evaluation. We report the \textit{local generalization} performance by averaging the pass rates of all templates

For the \textit{broad generalization} setting, the same testing templates used for the D-DDQN evaluation were used and the within scenario pass rate is calculated by averaging over all the tested templates within the scenario.

random_agent.text: We run the random agent 50 times per task and report the average pass rate of these 50 attempts.

dqn_local_setup.text: For the \textit{local generalization} evaluation, we run 10 sampling agents that use the same DQN model to collect experiences. Each sampling agent runs on the randomly selected task for 10 episodes. After the set of experiences is collected, the DQN model is trained for 10 epochs with a batch size of 32. We train DQN until it either converges or reaches $N$ update steps, where $N$ is the number of training tasks per template divided by 5.
We train our agent on 80$\%$ of the tasks of the task template and evaluate on the rest of the tasks of the same template.
At the testing time, the agent runs on each of the testing tasks only once and selects the action that has the highest Q-value for a given state.

local_split.text: For learning agents, we take the first 80 tasks from each task template as the training set and the last 20 tasks to evaluate the local generalization ability of the agent.

local_target_text.section: Local and Broad Generalization Performance and Phy-Q Score
local_target_text.text: While both the symbolic learning agents and both the image learning agents on average pass approximately $33\%$ and $24\%$ of the test levels respectively

compute.section: Computing Resources Used for the Experiments
compute.text: Four instances of vCPUs with 2.5 GHz processors and 16 GB memory were used. NVIDIA T4 GPUs with 16 GB memory were used in those instances.

definitions.human_average_rate: (6 - attempts)/5 if attempts <= 5 else 0 (README 'Play Data' item 5; paper Results 'Human Performance'); violations in data: 0
definitions.human_scenario_pass_rate: mean of average_rate over all (player, task) rows of the scenario
definitions.heuristic_task_pass_rate: mean over the task's attempts of LevelStatus == 'Pass' ('Playing' and 'Fail' count as not passed)
definitions.local_gen: mean over the 75 templates of the per-template pass rate
definitions.broad_gen_scenario: mean over the scenario's test templates (paper Supp. E) of the per-template pass rate
definitions.phyq: Z_agent = (1/13) sum_{m=3..15} (P_agent,m - P_human,m) / sigma_human,m; Phy-Q = 100 + Z_agent * 100/|Z_random| (main.tex lines 1344-1349, section 'Proposed Evaluation Settings')

findings: Phy-Q (primary definition): Bambirds 13.59, Eagle's Wing 12.11, Datalab 6.71, Pig Shooter -1.60, D-DDQN-Symbolic 6.42, D-DDQN-Image 8.76, Relational-Symbolic 8.40, Relational-Image 6.05; scaling factor 13.5754.

sigma_human: the released sd_human_pass_rate column equals the population SD (ddof=0) over the 19 players of each player's mean average_rate in the scenario; the paper only says 'standard deviation of human pass rate'.
Human data: 19 players released vs 20 stated in the paper; 10 task rows carry attempts = 100 (sentinel; average_rate 0).
Heuristic per-template pass rate = mean over a task's plays of (LevelStatus == 'Pass'), averaged over the template's tasks; the scenario broad-gen value averages the paper's test templates (Supp. E).
Bambirds was played on 0.229 of its tasks within 81-100 (the paper says heuristics used the learning agents' test 20%, i.e. tasks 81-100); 223 Bambirds tasks have 10 plays instead of 5.
Pig Shooter = raw file Naive.csv (its test-template scenario means equal the 'Pig Shooter' CSV rows except 2_03, see below).

Released heuristic scenario aggregates (the *_summarized_h_c.csv files and the Pig Shooter 2_03 cell of broad_generalization_all_agents.csv) pool tasks across templates; the paper says the scenario value averages the tested templates. The two differ only where a template has < 20 tasks (Naive, EagleWings, DataLab): Pig Shooter 2_03 broad gen 0.0100 (template mean) vs 0.0105 released (= pooled 0.0105).
Pig Shooter local gen 0.10508 (template mean) / 0.10632 (pooled) vs Fig. 4b 0.1050: neither definition reproduces it, while the template mean reproduces Bambirds, Eagle's Wing and Datalab to 4 d.p.

Human 1.86 attempts / 23.73 s per task (paper text): no candidate definition over the 19 released players reproduces them (human.attempts_candidates, human.think_time_candidates); [INFERENCE] they include the unreleased 20th player.
Phy-Q with sigma_human ddof=1 gives scaling factor 13.947 (paper 13.58), so the published Phy-Q used the population SD.

what_a_run_is.entry_point: sciencebirdsagents/TrainLearningAgent.py --template <L_CC_TT> --mode within_template --game_version Linux --level_path fifth_generation (one process per template; TrainLearningAgent.sh loops over Utils/GenerateTemplateName.py output)
what_a_run_is.networks: Utils/Parameters.py 'network': DQNRelationalSymbolic (default) or DQNRelationalImage; agent class DQNDiscreteAgent (180 discrete release angles, max stretch)
what_a_run_is.templates: 75 templates (fifth_generation.zip: 75 dirs x 100 task XMLs); a within-template run trains and tests on ONE template
what_a_run_is.train_test_split: Utils/Config.py update_level_index: tasks sorted by index, train = first int(0.8*100) = 80 (1..80), test = last 20 (81..100); paper Supp. D: 'first 80 ... last 20'
what_a_run_is.num_update_steps: Parameters.py sets 20 (40 cross-template) but TrainLearningAgent.py line 219 overrides it to len(train)//5 = 16 for level_path != 'MattewLevel'; paper: N = training tasks per template / 5 = 16
what_a_run_is.step_0_collection: level_per_agent=None and RepeatPlay(10) at step 0: every one of the 80 training tasks is played 10 times (800 episodes), split over the 10 workers (8 tasks each)
what_a_run_is.steps_1_to_15_collection: each of the 10 workers plays 1 task sampled from its 8 (random.sample) once: 10 episodes per step
what_a_run_is.early_stop: collection loop breaks if the mean winning rate of the step's episodes > 0.99
what_a_run_is.epochs_note: train_time_per_ep starts at 32 and is reduced cumulatively by step*train_time_rise (TrainLearningAgent.py line 224); the paper text says 10 epochs
what_a_run_is.reward_type: 'passing' (1 if the task is passed, else 0)
what_a_run_is.seed: 5123690 (python, numpy, torch); torch deterministic algorithms disabled; one run per template
what_a_run_is.evaluation: after training, each of the 20 test tasks is played once (RepeatPlay(1)) greedily (EPS_START=0); per-template metric = fraction of the 20 test tasks passed
what_a_run_is.episode: one task play: shots until WON/LOST (SBEnvironmentWrapper.step: one shot per step; is_done on WON/LOST); shots per episode is between 1 and the task's bird count

release_code_defects_observed_by_reading: Utils/Parameters.py sets 'agent': 'ppo' (a str) while TrainLearningAgent.py uses c.agent.__name__ and calls c.agent(...): the released defaults must be edited to DQNDiscreteAgent to run the DQN baselines [observed in source, not executed]
Utils/Parameters.py 'device' is cuda:0/cuda:1 unconditionally; a CPU-only run needs it changed [observed in source]
TrainLearningAgent.sh iterates 'for val in ${templates}' (bash array without [@]): only the first template (1_01_01) runs [observed in source]
TrainLearningAgent.py benchmark split lists '1_01_09' as a 2_01 training template (paper Table S: 3.3 = 2_01_09) [observed in source]

per_template.location: Supplementary D, Fig. 'Passing rates of the agents for the within template evaluation' (Fig_within_template_submission_2_avg_pass_rates.PNG, main.tex line 2268)
per_template.note: bar chart only (75 templates x 9 agents): no numeric values, no SD, no error bars; one run per template. Any per-template comparison is a visual bar reading (+-~0.05).

per_scenario_within_template.note: not reported (the Fig. S bars are grouped by scenario but no scenario means are given)

all_templates_mean.location: Fig. 4b row 'Local gen.' (Fig4_local_broad_gen.PNG); text: 'symbolic ... and image learning agents on average pass approximately 33% and 24%' (main.tex line 1454)
all_templates_mean.definition: mean over the 75 templates of the per-template pass rate on the 20 test tasks
all_templates_mean.sd: not reported (single run; no seeds or SD anywhere in the paper)

sampling_noise_[INFERENCE].note: test-set sampling noise only; training-run (seed) variance is unreported and comes on top

execution_counts.definition: execution = one engine shot (SBEnvironmentWrapper.step -> ar.shoot); lower bound = 1 shot per episode; upper bound = every episode uses all of the task's birds (bird counts from fifth_generation.zip; steps 1-15 use the mean bird count of the template's training tasks [INFERENCE: uniform random.sample]). Early stopping, stuck-level reloads (>15 shots) and level loads are not counted.

variants.code: released code as written (step 0: 80 x 10 episodes; steps 1-15: 10 x 1 x 1)
variants.paper_text: [INFERENCE] the paper's description taken literally: 16 steps x 10 agents x 10 episodes

execution_counts.smallest_credible_set: all_75_templates: the only numeric published within-template target is the 75-template mean (Fig. 4b). A per-template or one-per-scenario run can only be compared with bar heights read off Fig. S.

native_task_fidelity.worker_hours_formula: worker_hours = executions * seconds_per_execution / 3600 (game-instance hours; the 10 workers run in parallel, so wall-clock ~ worker_hours / 10)
